title: Unique Paths in Grid
statement: There is a robot on an m x n grid at top-left (0, 0). The robot can only move down or right. Return the number of possible unique paths to reach the bottom-right corner (m - 1, n - 1).
hints: First row and first column cells have only 1 unique path.
For any interior cell (r, c), paths[r][c] = paths[r - 1][c] + paths[r][c - 1].
Can be computed with a single 1D row of length n.

solutions.title: 1D Rolling Array DP
Combinatorics Formula

editorial.approach: 2D Grid DP with space optimization: let dp[c] be the number of unique paths to column c in the current row. Since moving is restricted to down and right, dp[c] = dp[c] + dp[c - 1]. Initialize a 1D array of size n with all 1s (top row). Iterate through the remaining m - 1 rows, updating dp[c] += dp[c - 1] for each column from 1 to n - 1.
editorial.why_optimal: Computes path counts in O(m * n) time and O(n) space, avoiding full 2D grid allocation while computing the combinatorial equivalent of C(m+n-2, m-1).
editorial.pitfalls: Off-by-one errors in row/column iterations. Using floating-point combinations for large m, n which causes precision inaccuracies.
